name: RankHive – AI SEO Agent: Search Console Fixes You Approve
author: 1729labs

sections.description:
RankHive reads your Google Search Console data and finds the work: pages ranking 5th to 20th, titles people see but don’t click, and pages losing clicks. It drafts each fix, such as a new title or meta description, internal links, schema, or image alt text. You approve, edit or discard each fix in the RankHive app. This plugin then writes the approved change to WordPress and logs the old value, so you can revert it from the Change Log.

Nothing on your site changes until you approve it. RankHive audits the site every week, and a fix that comes from your search data shows the Search Console numbers behind it.

Approved titles, meta descriptions and canonical URLs are written into Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO (AIOSEO) or SEOPress, whichever one is active, and that plugin outputs them as usual. You need one of those four active for title, description and canonical changes to show on your pages. Content, internal link, schema, image alt text, redirect and robots.txt changes work without one.

RankHive edits posts and pages. It does not edit WooCommerce product pages yet.

Free SEO check, no account needed. Open RankHive > SEO check and click Run check. It looks at up to 1,000 of your newest posts, pages and WooCommerce products and lists pages hidden from Google, links to pages on your site that don’t exist, missing and duplicate meta descriptions, duplicate titles, titles too long for Google, descriptions too short or too long, posts under 300 words and images without alt text. Each finding says why it matters and links to the posts to fix. The check reads your WordPress database only and sends nothing anywhere.

The plugin is free. RankHive is a paid service: $49.99 a month or $499.99 a year per WordPress site, after a 7-day free trial. You add a card when the trial starts; cancel before day 8 and you pay nothing. See pricing or read the FAQ.

This is an early access release. A RankHive account is required for AI analysis, approvals, reporting, scheduling, and WordPress writes.

The plugin handles:

  • a free SEO check of your posts, pages and products that runs without an account
  • secure site connection and credential storage
  • authenticated REST bridge for reads and guarded writes
  • writing approved titles, meta descriptions and canonical URLs into your SEO plugin’s fields
  • plugin-owned schema rendering
  • plugin-owned redirects and optional robots management
  • outbound webhook delivery for site events
  • operational dashboard, activity feed, and connection diagnostics

RankHive handles:

  • AI analysis and recommendations
  • approvals and change history
  • reporting, billing, scheduling, and user management
  • Google Search Console connection (read-only)

The plugin transmits site content and metadata to RankHive only after an administrator connects the site.

Privacy

RankHive – AI SEO Agent does not transmit site data until the administrator connects the plugin to RankHive. Once connected, the plugin may send site URLs, site metadata, active theme and plugin metadata, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions, post and page titles, slugs, URLs, excerpts, content, content hashes, SEO metadata, schema, taxonomies, featured image and media metadata, author display name and ID, headings, image references, internal links, plugin-managed redirects, robots data, webhook event metadata, diagnostics, and approved write results.

Connected reads can include published, draft, pending, private, and other requested post statuses when the RankHive workflow asks for them. RankHive uses this data only to provide the customer’s SEO service. RankHive stores data while the user is a customer, and users can delete site data from the RankHive dashboard.

The plugin stores connection settings, operational logs, optional render toggles and the last SEO check result locally in the WordPress database. The SEO check reads your database and sends nothing to RankHive or anyone else.

Read the RankHive Privacy Policy.

External service

This plugin connects to RankHive, a third-party SaaS operated by 1729 Labs. RankHive is a paid service; prices are in the Description above.

Service URL: www.rankhive.app

Privacy Policy: www.rankhive.app/privacy-policy

Terms of Service: www.rankhive.app/terms-of-service

A RankHive account is required to use AI analysis, approvals, reporting, scheduled checks, and approved WordPress changes. The plugin sends data to RankHive only after an administrator starts and approves the connection flow.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/rankhive-ai-seo-agent, or install it from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin. You will be taken to the RankHive screen automatically.
  3. Click “Connect your-site.com to RankHive” (it names your site).
  4. Sign in to RankHive or create an account. A new account also connects Google Search Console, chooses monthly or yearly billing and starts a 7-day free trial during setup. Approve this site, and you will be brought back to wp-admin automatically.
  5. Your first full audit starts once the site is connected and your trial has started. Its fixes wait in RankHive for your approval.

To see what needs fixing before you connect, open RankHive > SEO check and click Run check. It needs no account.
sections.faq:
What does RankHive cost?

The plugin is free. RankHive is a paid service: $49.99 a month or $499.99 a year per WordPress site, after a 7-day free trial. Every feature is included. Agencies add more sites from Settings in RankHive, each billed at the same price. See pricing.

Is there a free trial?

Yes. You get 7 days of the full product for one site, and your first full audit runs during it. You add a card at checkout. Cancel before day 8 and you pay nothing; otherwise your plan starts on day 8 at $49.99 a month or $499.99 a year. One trial per customer.

Does this plugin work without a RankHive account?

The SEO check does. Open RankHive > SEO check to see the problems on your posts, pages and products, each linked to its edit screen. Drafting and applying fixes, Search Console analysis, approvals and the Change Log need a connected RankHive account.

What does the free SEO check look at?

Up to 1,000 of your newest published posts, pages and WooCommerce products. It reads each one’s title, meta description and noindex setting from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress (with none of them active, it uses the title WordPress prints). It also checks the content for links to pages on your site that don’t exist, images without alt text and posts under 300 words. It runs only when you click Run check, reads your database only and sends nothing anywhere. The last result stays on the screen until you run it again.

Which SEO plugins does it work with?

Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO (AIOSEO, free and Pro) and SEOPress. Approved titles, meta descriptions and canonical URLs are written into the fields of whichever one is active, and that plugin outputs them as usual. With no SEO plugin, or a different one, those three changes are saved but don’t show on your pages. Content, internal link, schema, image alt text, redirect and robots.txt changes don’t depend on an SEO plugin.

Does it edit WooCommerce products?

Not yet. RankHive reads and edits posts and pages, such as a store’s blog posts and buying guides. It does not audit or edit WooCommerce product or category pages.

What access does RankHive need in Google?

Read-only access to Google Search Console, plus the email address of the Google account you connect. RankHive uses your search data to decide which fixes are worth making, and shows it next to the fixes it drives. It can’t change anything in your Search Console account.

What data is sent to RankHive?

RankHive may receive connection metadata, site metadata, content, SEO metadata, media metadata, author display names and IDs, redirects, robots data, webhook event metadata, diagnostics, and approved write results needed to provide the connected SEO service.

Can RankHive change my WordPress site?

Yes, but only after you approve the proposed change in RankHive. Approved changes can update SEO titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, content, internal links, schema, image alt text, post status, redirects, and robots.txt, and can create draft posts. The plugin cannot delete posts and does not touch your themes, plugins, or users.

Can I undo a change?

Yes, for titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, content and internal link edits, schema, image alt text, post status, redirects, and robots.txt. Click Revert in RankHive’s Change Log. A redirect RankHive created is switched off, because the plugin doesn’t delete redirects. If a paragraph, link, redirect, or robots.txt was edited after RankHive’s change, the revert stops and tells you instead of overwriting it. New article drafts can’t be reverted from the Change Log.

What happens if I cancel?

Changes RankHive already made stay on your site. You can cancel anytime from the billing settings in RankHive. Cancel during the 7-day trial and you pay nothing. After that, you keep access until the end of the period you paid for. Payments are not refunded, as the refund policy explains. Titles, descriptions, and content edits are saved in WordPress and your SEO plugin like any other edit. Schema, redirects, and robots.txt rules are served by this plugin, so they keep working while it is active. Deleting the plugin removes its redirects and settings, and its schema output stops.

Does the plugin render schema or robots output?

Yes. JSON-LD schema can be rendered from plugin-owned metadata, and robots output can be enabled from the settings screen when the site needs plugin-owned robots handling. If your SEO plugin already outputs structured data, you can turn off this plugin’s schema output in its Advanced settings to avoid duplicate markup.
sections.changelog:
0.1.6

  • New free SEO check under RankHive > SEO check. It needs no account and sends nothing anywhere. It lists pages hidden from Google, links to pages on your site that don’t exist, missing and duplicate meta descriptions, duplicate titles, titles too long for Google, descriptions too short or too long, posts under 300 words and images without alt text, each with links to the posts to fix.
  • After activation, the RankHive screen shows one button, “Connect your-site.com to RankHive”, and one sentence saying what it does. Nothing is sent to RankHive until you click it.
  • The notice after connecting says what happens next: your first audit is running, or checkout in RankHive comes first. It no longer says the first results are ready when they aren’t.

0.1.5

  • All in One SEO (free and Pro): approved titles, meta descriptions and canonical URLs are now saved in AIOSEO’s own post settings, so AIOSEO shows them on your pages. Earlier versions saved them where AIOSEO does not read them.
  • If AIOSEO is active but its data can’t be loaded, title, description and canonical changes are refused instead of saved where they won’t show. The plugin screen says where these changes are saved.
  • The robots.txt setting now says what it does: it adds your lines to the end of the robots.txt WordPress serves, and has no effect if your site has a physical robots.txt file.

0.1.4

  • Fix SEO meta writes clearing fields they were not changing: approving a title change no longer deletes the meta description and canonical (and vice versa), including on reverts. Only the fields a request carries are written, and unchanged values are no longer recorded as changes.
  • Keep backslashes in written content, alt text, redirects and robots.txt (e.g. code samples). Strings are stored as sent unless the request marks them as slashed.
  • A refused write (conflict, validation error) is no longer replayed for its idempotency key, so a retry after re-reading the post goes through.
  • Updating a redirect without an is_regex value keeps the rule’s current regex setting.

0.1.3

  • Fix outbound webhook delivery returning 401: the webhook signer now sends the API key id instead of the site id in the X-SEOAgent-Key-Id header, matching the signature used for all other authenticated requests.

0.1.2

  • Schedule posts natively in WordPress with optional publish_at (future status + post dates).
  • Fix status-only updates so publish/draft changes apply when publish_at is omitted.
  • Reset post dates when leaving a scheduled (future) post so drafts do not keep a future stamp.
  • Fall back to the first administrator as post author for HMAC API writes with no logged-in user.

0.1.1

  • Added authentication to the posts and robots read REST endpoints.
  • Added connection-callback state validation to prevent CSRF-style state changes on the admin screen.
  • Prefixed the activation transient to avoid naming collisions.
  • Updated the Author and Plugin URI to the RankHive site.

0.1.0

  • Initial early access release.

How it works: connect your site and Search Console, RankHive finds the work, you approve each fix, and every change is recorded.
Before and after RankHive: the SEO routine done by hand each week, and the same work as a weekly list of drafted fixes you approve.
